opening.argument: The presentation frames the money, bank-access, overpayment, and gift-card elements as the caller’s pressure tactics within a recorded interaction, not as an offer to viewers. Its description identifies an “aggressive tech support scammer” pressuring the speaker for $10,000, while the participants explicitly say, “We have to string them along.” The caller’s supposed $300 refund, bank-login instructions, alleged overpayment, and demand for Apple gift cards are therefore presented as material being investigated and prolonged. The livestream-style step bar and KITBOGA closing screen further contextualize the exchange as hosted content, and the statement that “they never transferred me any money at all” reinforces that the interaction is being examined rather than completed. The available evidence contains no request for viewers to send money, buy gift cards, provide credentials, or participate.

We have to string them along.
